note: MAPPING: data/hexaco_ashton_2014.r pivots select(starts_with('C')) by column NAME, so the live code IS the source column name (COrga1..CPrud10). starts_with() is case-insensitive, so it also catches 'country', but that column is renamed cov_country beforehand and excluded from the pivot; no other data.csv column starts with C/c. Live item set = the 40 C-codes exactly (validate_items.R --table-sets PASS). codebook.txt keys each code to its sentence one per line ('CPrud8 I make careless mistakes.'), 40/40 present, no duplicates. No positional step. INSTRUMENT (Step 3b): these are the IPIP-HEXACO scales (Ashton, Lee & Goldberg 2007), NOT the HEXACO-PI-R, despite the table description 'HEXACO Personality Inventory': all 40 stems match ipip.ori.org/newhexaco_pi_key.htm's Organization/Diligence/Perfectionism/Prudence keys once the codebook's 'I ' prefix is removed (40/40), with within-facet numbering following the key's order (+keyed first). Live-data polarity agrees item by item (each item vs the mean of its facet's other +keyed items, n=22786): Orga1..5 +0.26..+0.66, Orga6..10 -0.30..-0.57; Dili1..5 +0.44..+0.66, Dili6..10 -0.38..-0.60; Perf1..8 +0.45..+0.65, Perf9..10 -0.46/-0.23; Prud1..3 +0.28..+0.56, Prud4..10 -0.17..-0.31 -- 40/40 in the IPIP key's sign, so the stored data are raw, not reverse-scored. RIGHTS: register row HEXACO-PI-R (block, irw#1945) does not apply -- not this instrument. Applied the existing IPIP register verdict (ship): ipip.ori.org home page (fetched 2026-09-24 by batch_349, sha256 45d41652bdf7a434973b8501051272e2e8b764f588629fed96f22116d184cd0e): 'The items and scales are in the public domain, which means that one can copy, edit, translate, or use them for any purpose without asking permission and without paying a fee.' No new register row written. TEXT: item_text is the codebook sentence verbatim incl. its 'I ' prefix; all 40 read grammatically. One character-level deviation from the IPIP key, kept as the codebook prints it: COrga5 'I want everything to be just right.' (IPIP: 'Want everything to be "just right."', quotation marks absent in the codebook). ANCHORS: codebook header gives '1 = strongly disagree, 2 = disagree, 3 = slightly disagree, 4 = neutral, 5 = slightly disagree, 6 = agree, 7 = strongly agree'; 5 is an evident typo (duplicates 3 on a symmetric 7-point scale) and ships CORRECTED as 'slightly agree', same as hexaco_ashton_2014_a; the original test page 404s so the displayed label could not be confirmed. Anchors lowercase as printed. instructions blank: the codebook's lead sentence describes the rating scale for data users, not participant instructions. Raw 0 recoded to NA by the script; 27 NA rows of 911440 in the live table; every item uses all seven levels 1-7; every item has 22786 rows.
